extracted.intended_audience: NeurIPS reviewers (area chairs, reviewers, and program committee members assigned to review NeurIPS submissions)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reviewing NeurIPS submissions: reviewer responsibilities, procedural rules (conflicts, confidentiality, double-blind), review content and scoring rubrics (summary, strengths, weaknesses, correctness, clarity, related work, reproducibility, overall & confidence scores), and discussion/author-response expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are assigned around 4-6 submissions (unless specified smaller quota). Reviewers must review submissions, read author responses, discuss submissions and author responses with other reviewers and area chairs (ACs), and help make decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Log in to CMT as soon as you are notified to check conflicts and expertise. If uncomfortable reviewing a paper, fill out a note in CMT and communicate to the AC immediately so an alternate reviewer can be found. Engage actively in the discussion phase for assigned submissions. Reviews and meta-reviews will be made public after decisions (identities remain anonymous).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must check for conflicts of interest for assigned papers and update CMT accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As soon as assigned, log in to CMT to check for conflicts. Keep domain conflicts up to date in CMT; see linked "what constitutes conflict of interest for NeurIPS 2020" guidance. If you have a conflict, do not review; communicate promptly to your AC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: All aspects of the review process must be kept confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use ideas, code, or results from submissions in your own work until publicly available. Do not talk about or distribute submissions (code, ideas, results) without prior approval from program chairs. Submitted code cannot be distributed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-blind reviewing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewing process is double blind at the level of reviewers and ACs: reviewers and ACs cannot see author identities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not attempt to discover author identities (e.g., via Google or arXiv). If you accidentally find identities, do not divulge them. If a submission is not adequately anonymized (author names, affiliations, acknowledgements, or other identifying information present), contact the corresponding AC and do not try to de-anonymize authors. Authors are responsible for anonymizing submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary material policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may submit up to 100MB of supplementary material in PDF or ZIP format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers' responsibility is to read and review the submission itself; looking at supplementary material is at reviewer discretion. Because NeurIPS submissions are short, reviewers may wish to inspect supplementary material before criticizing insufficient details, proofs, or experimental results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executing code & clicking on links (security)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitted code and external links may be untrusted and contain vulnerabilities or leak information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If planning to run supplementary source code, do so in a secure environment: (1) inside a Docker container, (2) a Virtual Machine (VirtualBox/VMWare), or (3) on a network-isolated cloud instance. Be cautious about accessing web links provided from the paper; they may log visitor IPs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting instructions and page limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions are limited to eight content pages (including figures and tables) in the NeurIPS submission style; extra pages allowed only for broader impact and references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must use the NeurIPS 2020 LaTeX style file. If assigned submissions violate the NeurIPS style (e.g., decreased margins or font size) or page limits, notify the AC immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions identical or substantially similar to papers submitted to, accepted to, or published in other archival venues, or to other NeurIPS submissions, should be deemed dual submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sliced contributions may be considered dual submissions. If you suspect a dual submission or need clarification, contact the corresponding AC. See Call for Papers and FAQ for more details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review content — Summary and contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Briefly summarize the paper motivation, key contributions and achievements in a paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This helps ACs and authors determine misunderstandings and is invaluable for decision-making. Examples of acceptable contributions are provided in the guide (theoretical, methodological, empirical, connecting ideas, critical analyses, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Review content — Strengths
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the strengths of the work (typical criteria: soundness of claims, significance, novelty, relevance to NeurIPS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List strengths concretely (e.g., sound empirical methodology, theoretical grounding). Cite relevant prior work precisely when used to justify strengths. Consider significance as expected community uptake or influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review content — Weaknesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain the limitations of the work along the same axes as strengths (soundness, significance, novelty, relevance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be detailed, specific, and polite. Avoid vague subjective complaints. Help authors understand how to improve the work. Remember you're evaluating scientific contribution, not personal interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review content — Correctness
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the claims and methods are correct and whether empirical methodology is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorrect claims or methodology are primary reasons for rejection; thoroughly motivate criticism so authors can respond. Provide concrete examples of technical or methodological errors when found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review content — Clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Rate the clarity of exposition and whether the paper is well written.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give examples of which parts need revision. Suggest specific improvements (notation, missing equation numbers, organization). Clarity includes being well organized and informative enough for an expert to reproduce results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review content — Relation to prior work
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain whether the submission adequately discusses how it differs from previous contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Related work should not just list prior work but explain differences. Authors are excused for not knowing all non-refereed work; work appearing less than two months before the deadline is considered contemporaneous. For camera-ready versions, more detailed comparisons are encouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review content — Reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether there are enough details to reproduce the major results of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not reproducible, list lack of reproducibility among weaknesses. Consider whether code, data, hyperparameters, or proof details are sufficiently provided (in paper or supplementary).

rubrics_metrics.name: Review content — Additional feedback, questions, and suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional free-text area for additional comments, suggestions for improvement, and questions to authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this space for clarifications you'd like during author response or for improvement suggestions not covered elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall score (10–1 scale and guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign an overall score reflecting assessment of the submission’s contributions (10 = top 5% of accepted NeurIPS papers, down to 1 = trivial or wrong).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do NOT assume assigned papers are representative of the submission pool. Use the provided rubric: 10: Top 5% accepted (groundbreaking), 9: Top 15% accepted, 8: Top 50% accepted (very good), 7: Good (accept), 6: Marginally above threshold, 5: Marginally below threshold, 4: Okay but not good enough (reject), 3: Clear reject, 2: Strong reject (surprised it was submitted), 1: Trivial/wrong/already known. Provide supporting arguments for your score; ACs use these to make decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidence score (5–1 scale)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate how certain you are about your assessment (5: absolutely certain; 1: educated guess).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use descriptions: 5 very familiar with related work, 4 confident but not absolute, 3 fairly confident, 2 willing to defend but likely unfamiliar with central parts, 1 educated guess. Be honest about how much math/details were checked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broader impact statement adequacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether the authors have adequately addressed the broader impact of their work (positive and negative ethical/societal implications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer Yes/No/Only partially and explain. Authors are required to include a broader impact statement; consider whether its discussion is balanced and covers potential negative outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical concerns flagging
rubrics_metrics.description: Flag whether the submission raises potential ethical concerns (methods, applications, data causing unfair bias or primary purpose of harm).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer Yes or No and briefly explain. This flag is independent of your overall rating; if AC agrees, dedicated ethics reviewers may further review the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Previous review/resubmission disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Declare whether you have previously reviewed or area chaired a version of this work for another archival venue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer Yes/No. This helps ACs contextualize your review; ACs have access to authors' resubmission statements if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agree to abide by the NeurIPS code of conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must agree to follow the NeurIPS code of conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge the code (link provided). Reviews must accord with the code; avoid discriminatory or inappropriate language; use neutral phrasing for language/grammar suggestions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential comments to the area chair
rubrics_metrics.description: A text field for comments that should be kept confidential from the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for explicit comparisons to other submissions, blunt criticisms, or other comments you do not want disclosed to authors. You may also disclose that you accidentally learned author identities here (but do not divulge to others).

rubrics_metrics.name: Author response handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must read author responses and (if appropriate) update their reviews and indicate whether they agree or disagree with the response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not ignore any author response. If your opinion remains the same, explain why specifically rather than writing only "I have read the author response and my opinion remains the same." Update the review to reflect consideration of the response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion phase participation
rubrics_metrics.description: After author response, AC will initiate discussion; reviewers should participate to reach consensus where possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discussion is especially important for borderline or conflicting reviews. Consider other reviewers' perspectives and change your mind if appropriate; consensus is valuable but not mandatory. Be professional and polite in discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer best practices (tone, fairness, availability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer conduct expectations: be fair, thoughtful, constructive, professional, and avoid discriminatory comments; notify AC if unavailable for important windows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid comments implying an author is "foreign" or "non-native"; use neutral formulations for English/style suggestions. If unavailable for more than a few days (especially during discussion), inform your AC. Do not discuss assigned submissions with others without AC permission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of review content (illustrative examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: The guide provides many example quotes illustrating good and bad review content for Contributions, Quality, Clarity, Originality, Significance, and concrete technical critique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the examples as models for writing thorough, specific, and constructive reviews. Examples illustrate how to point out technical errors, unclear exposition, related-work omissions, and trade-offs in significance vs novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: AC evaluation of review quality and reviewer rewards
rubrics_metrics.description: ACs will evaluate each review with three scores: "exceeded expectations", "met expectations", and "failed to meet expectations."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Top 8% of reviewers (highest scores) receive free NeurIPS registrations; the next top 30% have registrations reserved for a limited time. Low-scoring reviewers may not be invited in future.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of TPMS and OpenReview / profile upkeep
rubrics_metrics.description: NeurIPS uses TPMS and OpenReview to assign submissions; reviewers should keep profiles up to date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Log into TPMS and OpenReview to ensure your profile (areas of expertise) is current; stale profiles cause poor assignments. Update contact info and domain conflicts in CMT to avoid assignment issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: CMT email and communication protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Most conference emails are sent from CMT (email@msr-cmt.org); reviewers will receive many CMT emails during the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check spam folders and whitelist the CMT email address. Do not reply directly to CMT emails; instead use the "email meta-reviewer" and "email senior meta-reviewer" links on CMT to send messages.
